description: This repo dogfoods its own org-shared preset (default.json, consumed elsewhere as `github>FS-GG/.github`) instead of vanilla config:recommended, so the dist/dotnet pins it distributes are managed under the same semantics every product repo gets — dependency dashboard, semantic commits, and FS.GG.* feed/grouping/prerelease routing (review M9, #132).

This file used to carry a `hostRules` block supplying `{{ secrets.FSGG_PACKAGES_READ_TOKEN }}` for nuget.pkg.github.com, on the stated premise that `FS.GG.* are not on nuget.org`. THAT PREMISE WAS FALSE — all 32 of the 32 packages the org publishes to GitHub Packages are also public on nuget.org, anonymously readable, at the same latest version (verified id-by-id against api.nuget.org, #576). The token was never needed; it also never resolved, because it names a Mend App Secret that no CI credential can read or verify.

The block is REMOVED rather than left inert, because it was not merely redundant — it is the sentence that stopped four people from checking. The FS.GG.SDD.Cli pin froze at 0.2.1 (#127), at 0.5.0 (#263), at 0.9.0 (#566), and again at 0.10.0; each freeze was hand-advanced and closed, because the config 'obviously' already had the token. A 401 on a Renovate datasource is not an error, it is an empty version list, so the bot detected the dependency, enumerated nothing, and opened no PR. The preset now routes FS.GG.* to nuget.org (default.json), which needs no credential at all.

CI's restore is a DIFFERENT mechanism on a different credential and is untouched: .github/workflows/contract-coherence.yml restores FS.GG.SDD.Cli from GitHub Packages using GITHUB_TOKEN with `packages: read`, which works. Only Renovate's datasource lookups moved.
